data.why: A backyard swimming pool built in the yard cut: we open close on the hole filling with water, watch it drain into the soil, then line it with a concrete shell, and the algae problem is fixed by a pump, pipes and a sand filter tank beside the pool, with the camera moving from the pool to the equipment and back to home view for the fence, bushes and young trees.

ideas.idea: dig a deep hole in the yard and fill it with water, and that is a pool
the ground drinks the water, so a pool-sized hole drains empty into the soil
a sprayed concrete shell on the floor and walls holds the water in
leaves and dirt fall in and the still water turns green
a pump pushes the water through pipes into a tank of sand
the pump and sand tank together are a pool filter
the pump pulls water from the floor, sand traps the dirt, and clean water returns, cycling all of it every eight hours
everyone thinks the strong chlorine smell means a clean pool, but the smell is not chlorine itself
the smell is chlorine stuck to sweat and oils, so a truly clean pool barely smells
a fence, bushes and young trees complete the pool and keep it safe
the pool stands calm and clear, so you have built a swimming pool

chain.shows: the water level falls away and soaks down into the wet soil under the hole
chain.stakes: a 20,000 gallon pool is gone and the pool sits empty

chain.shows: leaves and mud drop in and the still water turns green
chain.stakes: the pool is unusable and unhealthy to swim in

surprises.claim: A typical backyard pool holds roughly 15,000 to 20,000 gallons of water.
surprises.search: average backyard swimming pool volume gallons

surprises.claim: Most in-ground pool shells are gunite or shotcrete, concrete that is sprayed through a hose.
surprises.search: gunite pool shell sprayed concrete shotcrete

surprises.claim: A pool pump is sized to cycle all the pool water through the filter about once every 8 hours.
The strong chlorine smell at pools comes from chloramines, chlorine that has bonded with sweat, urine and oils.
